lambeosaurus:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General non-avian dinosaur research)

facts.statement: William A. Parks named the genus Lambeosaurus in 1923.
facts.quote: authority: Parks, 1923

facts.statement: The type species of Lambeosaurus is Lambeosaurus lambei.
facts.quote: type_species: Lambeosaurus lambei

facts.statement: Two other species, L. magnicristatus and L. clavinitialis, were named by Sternberg in 1935.
facts.quote: subdivision: L. magnicristatus Sternberg, 1935 L. clavinitialis? Sternberg, 1935

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in western North America.
facts.quote: Lambeosaurus ( ) is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of western North America.

facts.statement: Lawrence M. Lambe originally used the first Lambeosaurus skull to justify creating the genus Stephanosaurus, though it was not part of that genus's original material.
facts.quote: The first skull of Lambeosaurus found was used by palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe to justify the creation of the new genus Stephanosaurus, although it was not part of the latter's original material.

facts.statement: William A. Parks named Lambeosaurus lambei in 1923 to honor Lawrence M. Lambe.
facts.quote: Its incomplete nature led William A. Parks to name Lambeosaurus lambei for this skull in 1923 to honour Lambe.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus is the eponymous member of the subfamily Lambeosaurinae and the tribe Lambeosaurini.
facts.quote: It is the eponymous member of the subfamily Lambeosaurinae and tribe Lambeosaurini.

facts.statement: Adult Lambeosaurus grew to about 7 to 7.7 meters long and weighed between 2.6 and 3.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Adult Lambeosaurus would have grown to around 7 - 7.7 m long and weighed 2.6 - 3.4 tonnes.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus could move on two or four legs and had a deep tail, long limbs, and a distinct hollow cranial crest.
facts.quote: It was able to move on two or four legs, with a deep tail, long limbs, and a highly distinct, hollow cranial crest.

facts.statement: Modern studies suggest the crest was used as a resonating device for vocalization and for sexual or species identification.
facts.quote: The function of the crest, which is also found in other lambeosaurines, is debated historically, but modern studies show that it could have been used as a resonating device for vocalisation, with a secondary function of sexual or species identification.

facts.statement: Skin impressions show that Lambeosaurus had unornamented scales across its entire body.
facts.quote: Skin impressions are known and show that it had unornamented scales across the entire body.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus species are known only from the middle Campanian of the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: The species of Lambeosaurus are only known from the middle Campanian of the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus lived in a coastal plain with meandering rivers, dense vegetation of conifers and ferns, and diverse invertebrates, fish, mammals, and reptiles.
facts.quote: The habitat Lambeosaurus lived in was a coastal plain where meandering rivers separated regions of dense vegetation, covered in a diversity of conifers, ferns and other shrubs, and occupied by diverse invertebrates, fish, mammals and reptiles, especially other megaherbivorous dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Geological Survey of Canada expeditions in the 1880s and 1890s discovered dinosaur fossils along the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: In the 1880s and 1890s, expeditions of the Geological Survey of Canada into Alberta discovered that the rocks along the Red Deer River bore dinosaur fossils of scientific importance.

facts.statement: Lawrence M. Lambe undertook three expeditions in 1897, 1898, and 1901 to badlands between Berry Creek and Deadlodge canyon.
facts.quote: Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence M. Lambe undertook three expeditions in 1897, 1898 and 1901 to an extensive series of badlands between Berry Creek and Deadlodge canyon.

facts.statement: Charles Hazelius Sternberg discovered multiple hadrosaur skeletons during a 1913 Geological Survey expedition.
facts.quote: A 1913 expedition of the Geological Survey to the same location resulted in the discovery of multiple hadrosaur skeletons by American palaeontologist Charles Hazelius Sternberg.

facts.statement: Specimen CMN 351, found 3.5 miles southeast of the mouth of Berry Creek, was described by Lambe in 1914.
facts.quote: One of these specimens (CMN 351), found by Sternberg 3.5 mi southeast of the mouth of Berry Creek, was described by Lambe more thoroughly later in 1914.

facts.statement: Lambe assigned skull CMN 2869 to Stephanosaurus in 1920, noting differences from Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1920, Lambe assigned another, even more complete skull (CMN 2869) to Stephanosaurus that showed differences to Corythosaurus.

facts.statement: William A. Parks designated Lambeosaurus lambei for skulls CMN 351 and CMN 2869 in 1923 because they could not be assigned to Stephanosaurus.
facts.quote: However, Canadian palaeontologist William A. Parks noted that Brown's logic still applied, and designated the new genus and species Lambeosaurus lambei for the complete skulls CMN 351 and CMN 2869 in 1923, as they could not justifiably be assigned to Stephanosaurus.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore described the type material of Lambeosaurus in 1924.
facts.quote: In 1924, American palaeontologist Charles W. Gilmore described the type material of Lambeosaurus in more detail.

facts.statement: A skull (FMNH UC 1479) was collected in 1926 by Levi Sternberg.
facts.quote: a skull (FMNH UC 1479) collected in 1926 by Levi Sternberg (son of C.H. Sternberg)

facts.statement: A skeleton missing the skull (FMNH PR 380) was collected in 1922, originally identified as Prosaurolophus, and later mounted as a Lambeosaurus scavenged by Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: and a skeleton missing the skull (FMNH PR 380) collected in 1922 by an expedition of the Field Museum of Natural History, which was originally identified as Prosaurolophus before being prepared and mounted as a Lambeosaurus being scavenged by Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: It is now known that the skull and skeleton previously thought to belong to the same individual were found 6 miles apart.
facts.quote: It was earlier believed that the skull and skeleton could have belonged to the same individual, but it is now known that they were found 6 mi apart.

facts.statement: American Museum of Natural History excavations in the Red Deer River region were conducted primarily by Brown between 1909 and 1914.
facts.quote: The American Museum of Natural History also excavated in the Red Deer River region, primarily through the work of Brown from 1909 to 1914.

facts.statement: American paleontologist William Diller Matthew assigned a small individual discovered by Brown to the genus Procheneosaurus in 1920.
facts.quote: One particularly small individual discovered by Brown, was assigned to as "Procheneosaurus" by American palaeontologist William Diller Matthew in 1920

facts.statement: Parks described small, crested hadrosaurs found by University of Toronto expeditions in the Red Deer badlands in 1931.
facts.quote: In 1931, Parks described more small, crested hadrosaurs found by expeditions of the University of Toronto into the Red Deer badlands.

facts.statement: Specimen ROM 3577 was found around 2 miles southeast of Little Sandhill Creek by L. Sternberg.
facts.quote: The first (ROM 3577) was found around 2 mi southeast of Little Sandhill Creek by L. Sternberg.

facts.statement: Specimen ROM 3578 was found in 1927 by L. Sternberg approximately 1.5 miles downriver of Little Sandhill Creek.
facts.quote: The second specimen, ROM 3578, was found in 1927 by L. Sternberg around 1.5 mi downriver of Little Sandhill Creek.

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg found the skull and skeleton CMN 8703, used to name L. clavinitialis, in 1928 about 2.5 miles south of the mouth of Berry Creek.
facts.quote: L. clavinitialis was named for a skull and skeleton (CMN 8703) that Sternberg found nearby, also in 1928, ca. 2.5 mi south of the mouth of Berry Creek.

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg found the mostly complete skull and skeleton CMN 8705, used to name L. magnicristatum, in 1919 about 3 miles southwest of the mouth of Little Sandhill Creek.
facts.quote: L. magnicristatum was named for a mostly complete skull and skeleton (CMN 8705) Sternberg found in 1919, about 3 mi southwest of the mouth of Little Sandhill Creek.

facts.statement: Lull and Wright assigned ROM 1218 to L. lambei; it was collected in 1920 by Levi Sternberg 1.5 miles northeast of Happy Jack Ferry.
facts.quote: L. lambei they assigned CMN 2869, ROM 5131, and ROM 1218, the second collected in 1920 by Levi Sternberg 1.5 mi northeast of Happy Jack Ferry, and the latter collected in the 1919 expedition on the south side of Red Deer River.

facts.statement: Specimen YPM 3222 was found in 1919 by C.M. Sternberg 3 miles south of the mouth of Little Sandhill Creek and included in L. clavinitialis.
facts.quote: L. clavinitialis included the specimens CMN 8703, CMN 351, and YPM 3222, the latter found in 1919 by C.M. Sternberg 3 mi south of the mouth of Little Sandhill Creek.

facts.statement: C.M. Sternberg opposed the use of Procheneosaurus in 1953, believing it to be a nomen nudum and retaining species in the genus Tetragonosaurus.
facts.quote: However, C.M. Sternberg had opposed in 1953 the use of Procheneosaurus over Tetragonosaurus as advocated by Lull and Wright, instead retaining all the species in the latter genus and believing "Procheneosaurus" to be a nomen nudum as suggested by Matthew.

facts.statement: William J. Morris argued that very little separates Lambeosaurus, Corythosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus beyond skull anatomy, making identification of non-skull material difficult.
facts.quote: American palaeontologist William J. Morris even argued that there is very little that separates Lambeosaurus, Corythosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus beyond the anatomy of the skull, preventing a confident identification of any material that lacks the skull.

facts.statement: David B. Norman and Hans-Dieter Sues argued that Jaxartosaurus was too distinct in time and space from Procheneosaurus convincens to be assigned to any known genus.
facts.quote: British and American palaeontologists David B. Norman and Hans-Dieter Sues, on the other hand, argued that Jaxartosaurus was too separate in time and space from Procheneosaurus convincens, and that although its validity was questionable, it could not be assigned to any known genera.

facts.statement: David C. Evans and colleagues found that the type specimen of Tetragonosaurus cranibrevis showed Lambeosaurus anatomy, making it a synonym of Lambeosaurus instead of Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: However, the type of T. cranibrevis showed the anatomy of Lambeosaurus, making the species a synonym of Lambeosaurus rather than Corythosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2007 redescription by David C. Evans and Robert R. Reisz showed that Lambeosaurus magnicristatus can be separated from L. lambei based on anatomy and geologically younger age.
facts.quote: The 2007 redescription showed that L. magnicristatus can be separated from L. lambei based on its anatomy as well as on its geologically younger age.

facts.statement: Albert Prieto-Márquez and colleagues found that ?Lambeosaurus laticaudus was distant from Lambeosaurus species and renamed it the new genus Magnapaulia.
facts.quote: It was more distant from the species of Lambeosaurus, and showed enough anatomical differences that they gave it the new genus name Magnapaulia.

facts.statement: In 2013, Kristin S. Brink and Phil R. Bell redescribed Procheneosaurus convincens and renamed it the new genus Kazaklambia due to differences from other lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Similarly, the skull of Procheneosaurus convincens was redescribed by Brink and Canadian palaeontologists Phil R. Bell in 2013, who found that it could be differentiated from other lambeosaurines of similar age including Jaxartosaurus, giving if the new genus name Kazaklambia.

facts.statement: Kazaklambia (formerly Procheneosaurus convincens) is an early member of Lambeosaurini and is only distantly related to Lambeosaurus.
facts.quote: It has been found to be an early member of Lambeosaurini and only distantly related to Lambeosaurus.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus is distinguished from other hadrosaurids mainly by its skull and crest, while sharing similar anatomy with relatives like Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: Lambeosaurus is primarily distinguished from other hadrosaurids by its skull and crest, otherwise being very close in anatomy to its close relatives Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus was a large hadrosaurid with grinding teeth, a stiffened tail, and semi-quadrupedal limbs, a locomotion style supported by footprints of related animals.
facts.quote: It was a large hadrosaurid, with highly developed jaws full of grinding teeth, a long tail stiffened by ossified tendons that prevented it from drooping, and more elongate limbs suggesting they were semi-quadrupedal (could move on both two legs and all fours), as also shown by footprints of related animals.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus hands had four fingers without a thumb, where the little finger was free and possibly used for manipulating objects.
facts.quote: The hands had four fingers, lacking the thumb, and while the second, third, and fourth fingers were bunched together, the little finger was free and could have been used to manipulate objects.

facts.statement: Each foot of Lambeosaurus had only the three central toes.
facts.quote: Each foot had only the three central toes.

facts.statement: L. lambei, L. magnicristatus, and L. clavinitialis reached approximately 7 to 7.7 meters in length and 2.6 to 3.4 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: L. lambei, L. magnicristatus, and L. clavinitialis would have reached around 7 - 7.7 m in length, and 2.6 - 3.4 tonnes in weight.

facts.statement: Skin impressions of Lambeosaurus have been preserved on the neck, pelvis, legs, and tail.
facts.quote: Lambeosaurus is also one of many hadrosaurs to preserve the impressions of skin, which has been found across the neck, pelvis, legs, and tail.

facts.statement: The skull of Lambeosaurus is distinct for its elaborate, narrow, and tall crest.
facts.quote: The skull of Lambeosaurus is particularly distinct, bearing an elaborate, narrow and tall crest.

facts.statement: Almost the entire crest of Lambeosaurus is formed by the premaxillae, which elongated and expanded to rearrange the skull roof bones.
facts.quote: Almost all of the crest is formed by the premaxillae of the snout, which have elongated and expanded over the skull in a way that has rearranged the other bones of the skull roof.

facts.statement: S-shaped looping passages inside the crest connect the external and internal nostrils, expanding the crest on both sides.
facts.quote: Inside the crests there are S-shaped looping passages that connect the external nares (nostrils) with the internal nares, which expand the crest on either side.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus teeth are tall relative to their width, have faint edge crenellations, and a single strong central keel.
facts.quote: The teeth of both jaws are typical for lambeosaurines, being very tall relative to their width, having very faint crenellations along their edges, and showing a single strong keel along the center.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus was described in 1923 by William Parks, over twenty years after Lawrence Lambe first studied the material.
facts.quote: Lambeosaurus fue tardíamente descrito en 1923 por William Parks, más de veinte años después de que el primer material fuera estudiado por Lawrence Lambe.

facts.statement: The genus Lambeosaurus was established by Parks in 1923.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Parks, 1923

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus magnicristatus (Sternberg, 1935) and Lambeosaurus paucidens (Marsh, 1889) are recognized subdivisions, with the latter being doubtful.
facts.quote: subdivision: Lambeosaurus magnicristatus Sternberg, 1935 Lambeosaurus paucidens Marsh, 1889 (dudosa)

facts.statement: Didanodon (Osborn, 1902), Procheneosaurus (Parks, 1920), and Tetragonosaurus (Parks, 1931) are listed as synonyms of Lambeosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Didanodon Osborn, 1902 Procheneosaurus Parks, 1920 Tetragonosaurus Parks, 1931

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus was a herbivore that walked quadrupedally but could stand on its hind legs, known for its distinctive hatchet-shaped hollow crest.
facts.quote: Este herbívoro que caminaba en posición cuadrúpeda, pero que podía erguirse en sus dos patas traseras es conocido por su cresta distintiva, en forma de hacha, cresta hueca.

facts.statement: It is debated whether certain skulls assigned to Lambeosaurus lambei represent developmental differences or sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Actualmente, varios cráneos asignados a la especie tipo Lambeosaurus lambei se ven como ejemplos de diferencias de desarrollo y dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus lambei closely resembled Corythosaurus except for the shape of its main head crest.
facts.quote: El Lambeosaurus más conocido, L. lambei, era muy similar al más famoso Corythosaurus en todo menos en la forma del adorno principal de la cabeza.

facts.statement: Compared to Corythosaurus, the Lambeosaurus crest was positioned further forward, formed by a larger forward-pointing square portion and a small backward spine, with hollow nasal passages stacked vertically at the front.
facts.quote: Comparado a Corythosaurus, la cresta de Lambeosaurus estaba más hacia adelante formada por una porción cuadrada mayor apuntando hacia adelante, y una pequeña espina hacia atrás, y los pasos nasales huecos dentro estaban en el frente de la cresta y apilados verticalmente.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the varying sizes and shapes of the crest depended on age and sex, with juveniles lacking it entirely.
facts.quote: Se supone que los diferentes tamaños y formas de este órgano dependían de la edad y el sexo, con los más jóvenes careciendo de él.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the nasal cavity structure improved the sense of smell or created a loud bellowing sound.
facts.quote: Se cree que esto pudo haber mejorado el sentido del olfato, o creado un fuerte balido.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature, the crest, differed between the two best-known species.
facts.quote: La característica más distintiva, la cresta, era diferente en las dos especies mejor conocidas.

facts.statement: In L. lambei, the crest was axe-shaped in fully grown animals, shorter and rounder in specimens considered to be females.
facts.quote: En L. lambei, tenía forma de hacha cuando el animal estaba completamente crecido, siendo más corta y redondeada en ejemplares considerados hembras.

facts.statement: In L. magnicristatus, the crest had a reduced handle and an expanded blade, forming a pompous Pompadour-style crest.
facts.quote: En L. magnicristatus, el "mango" estaba muy reducido, y la "hoja" expandida, formando una pomposa cresta tipo Pompadour.

facts.statement: The Canadian species of Lambeosaurus was approximately 9.5 meters long, similar in size to Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: La especie canadiense de Lambeosaurus parece tener un tamaño similar al de Corythosaurus, alrededor de 9,5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Scale impressions assigned to L. lambei show thin, uniform skin with polygonal scales distributed without a specific order on the neck, torso, and tail.
facts.quote: Impresiones de escamas son conocidas en varios especímenes, los cuales son ahora asignados a L. lambei tenía una piel fina y uniforme, con escamas poligonales con una distribución en ninguna sin un orden particular en el cuello, torso, y cola.

facts.statement: Footprint evidence indicates that Lambeosaurus exhibited gregarious behavior.
facts.quote: Por medio de sus huellas se ha descubierto que presentaban un comportamiento gregario.

facts.statement: They were fast animals, which was likely their only defense against carnivores alongside their large size.
facts.quote: Se trataba de animales rápidos, lo que era probablemente su única defensa contra los carnívoros, junto con su gran tamaño.

facts.statement: The taxonomic history of Lambeosaurus began in 1902 when Lawrence Lambe named a new hadrosaurid species from Alberta as Trachodon marginatus.
facts.quote: Lambeosaurus posee una complicada historia taxonómica, comenzando en 1902 cuando Lawrence Lambe nombró una nueva especie de hadrosáurido, originalmente GSC 419, de Alberta como Trachodon marginatus.

facts.statement: Paleontologists began finding better hadrosaurid remains from the same rocks in 1910, now known as the Late Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos comenzaron a encontrar mejores restos de hadrosáuridos de las mismas rocas en 1910, en lo que hoy se conoce como la Formación Dinosaur Park del Campaniano Tardío en el Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: In 1923, William Parks proposed a new genus and species for the skulls, naming Lambeosaurus lambei in honor of the deceased Lawrence Lambe, with the type specimen NMC 2869.
facts.quote: En 1923 William Parks propone un nuevo género y especie para los cráneos, ambos, el nombre genérico y específico rindiéndole honores a Lambe, fallecido 4 años antes, de Lambeosaurus lambei colocando de espécimen tipo NMC 2869, originalmente GSC 2869.

facts.statement: In the same publication, this species became the type genus of the new subfamily Lambeosaurinae, replacing the preexisting Stephanosaurinae.
facts.quote: En la misma publicación, esta especie se convirtió en el género tipo de la nueva subfamilia Lambeosaurinae , como reemplazo de la Stephanosaurinae preexistente.

facts.statement: Procheneosaurus praeceps and altidens are considered modern synonyms of Lambeosaurus lambei, although both names predate it.
facts.quote: Procheneosaurus praeceps y altidens son considerados sinónimos más modernos de Lambeosaurus lambei, aunque ambos precedan ese nombre.

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus belongs to the parent group Corythosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Corythosaurini

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Lambeosaurus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Procheneosaurus convence from Late Cretaceous Kazakhstan is a synonym of Jaxartosaurus aralensis or deserves its own genus.
facts.quote: El "Procheneosaurus" convence, del Cretácico tardío de Kazajistán, es conocido por un esqueleto casi completo al que le falta solo el hocico y el extremo de la cola. Fue nombrado por A. K. Rozhdestvensky en 1968. A veces se lo ha considerado sinónimo de Jaxartosaurus aralensis, o merecedor de su propio género.

facts.statement: In 2013, Bell and Brink designated P. convence as the type species of the new genus Kazaklambia.
facts.quote: Bell y Brink en 2013 hicieron "P". convence a la especie tipo del nuevo género Kazaklambia.
